Hi Lena — thanks again for the sync earlier today. Quick recap and the artifacts I promised: 

Summary of needs (my read):
- Clinical summarization for discharge notes (200–800 tokens output, average 400)
- Hard p99 latency target: <= 250ms for single-request inference in our pilot window
- Throughput: ~120 TPS steady with 300 TPS bursts for batch jobs
- Data residency: US-only; audit logs and retention controls required

Redwood fit scorecard (high-level recommendations):
- Candidate A: RWX-13B-quant (recommended for accuracy-cost sweet spot)
  - Verified (Redwood profile): 95 TPS single-instance throughput (batching enabled), median token latency 38ms, p95 token latency 120ms, p99 token latency 240ms at your target sequence lengths
- Candidate B: Redwood-3-small (lighter, lower cost)
  - Verified: 180 TPS (with continuous batching), median token latency 22ms, p95 75ms, p99 180ms

Notes on trade-offs:
- RWX-13B-quant gives better summarization coherence on clinical text and higher tolerance to prompt noise; expect ~5–8% higher cost vs Redwood-3-small but ~6–10pts lift in ROUGE/ROUGE-L/clinical fidelity in our evals
- Redwood-3-small is attractive for throughput and cost; may need prompt engineering and guardrails for hallucination on edge cases

Attached:
- medivue-bench-summary-20260714.csv (bench table with per-model TPS and latency percentiles)
- medivue-prompt-pack-20260714.json (sample prompt/temperature templates and evaluation queries)

Links (read-only):
- Quick bench landing: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/MV-9471
- Full report (HTML): https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-bench/MV-9471/full-report.html
- Prompt pack (Drive): https://drive.google.com/fake/prompt-pack-MV-9471

Immediate next steps I suggest:
1) Share these artifacts with your ML/data team and procurement (Jerome?)
2) If acceptable, we spin up a short pilot (2 weeks) scoped to 100 TPS steady with a canary route and rollback on quality regressions
3) Diego/Monica to build a mutual action plan (MAP) + pilot SOW; I'll include a recommended SLO (p99 <= 250ms, quality guardrails: threshold on clinical-F1 and hallucination rate)

Availability: I have 2 slots tomorrow 10:00–10:30am PT and 3:30–4:00pm PT. If neither works, send a couple of times and I’ll coordinate.

Thanks — Diego

Great questions — quick answers below (see inline):

> On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 3:27 PM Lena Park <lena.park@medivue.com> wrote:
> 1) For the p99 numbers you quoted, is that per-token p99 or end-to-end request p99 at ~400 tokens output?

Response: The numbers in the CSV are token-latency percentiles measured inside our runtime. For common batch sizes and the 400-token sequence we observe these token-level p99s translate to end-to-end p99s of ~220–260ms for RWX-13B-quant (your median case) and ~160–200ms for Redwood-3-small. The full-report.html includes the exact conversion table (section 3.2).

> 2) Do you have a sample cost estimate for the two candidates at our projected traffic (100 TPS steady, 300 TPS bursts)?

Response: Yes — rough monthly run-rate estimate (compute + networking):
- RWX-13B-quant: ~$18k–22k / month (pilot config, reserved baseline + burst allowance)
- Redwood-3-small: ~$10k–13k / month
These figures assume Redwood Managed serving with autoscaling policy and continuous batching. We can provide a formal cost worksheet once we confirm retention and KV-cache settings.

I've attached a trace snapshot for a 400-token run (p99-traces.png) and added a short appendix in the CSV describing the test harness and tokenization details.

Next: if you want, we can stand up a pilot image with both candidates in parallel (A/B) and collect a 48–72 hour regression signal against your prompt set; that will give you a direct quality delta.

Thanks — Diego
